clue.text: All hands to mow the crop

parts.note: all hands on a ship make up its crew
to mow grass is to cut it

explanation.surface: A captain orders the whole ship's company out to harvest the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-cropped short haircut is a crop, and this style is the classic example of one.

clue.text: Hand over the church keys

parts.note: CE is short for Church of England
D and E are two musical keys

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders the keys of the church building.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede territory or rights is to give them up, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Set a new course, perhaps

indicators.note: a new version of these letters is a fresh arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A navigator plots a different route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SETA into the compass point; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a course to steer.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass direction such as this one is a course a ship might steer.

clue.text: Single reed blown in the wind

definitions.text: Single reed blown in the wind

parts.words: Single reed blown in the wind
parts.note: reads like one stalk tossed by a breeze, but describes a woodwind instrument played with a single reed

explanation.surface: A lone reed bends in the breeze by the water.
explanation.definitionFit: This woodwind instrument has a single reed and belongs to the wind section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Tom came up with it, it's understood

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tom arrived with the item, and everyone simply knew it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is implied or understood without being spoken.

clue.text: Re-dial correctly, or get off the line

indicators.note: dialling correctly means putting these letters into their right order

explanation.surface: Advice on a wrong number: dial again properly or hang up.
explanation.definitionFit: A train that leaves the rails comes off the line, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: I enter amended total

indicators.note: amended means altered, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper types in a corrected sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire and total are synonyms meaning whole or complete.

clue.text: Bill gets a medical qualification from college

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: a qualification modifies or alters something, so these letters are changed

explanation.surface: A student named Bill earns a medical degree from his college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'qualification' looks like a degree here but works as the anagram signal, since to qualify a thing is to modify it; AC for account is the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Academical is an older adjective for things belonging to a college or university, such as academical dress.

clue.text: Not a working-class consumer

parts.note: sounds like a social category, but describes a person from Greek myth who eats a fruit that makes them idle

explanation.surface: A shopper described as not from the labouring classes.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey the lotus fruit made those who ate it forget work and home, so such an eater is literally not working.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler who lives in dreamy indulgence, after the fruit-eaters in Homer who abandoned all effort.

clue.text: Reserve takes ball and it's thrown in

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: letters that are thrown are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A substitute player gets the ball and throws it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' turns IT'S into IST, which goes 'in' DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve in the sense of aloofness or coolness is distance between people.

clue.text: Channel is without water, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the answer sounds like another word

parts.note: a drink taken straight has no water added

explanation.surface: A remark that a stretch of sea has dried out.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow channel of water joining two seas.

clue.text: Spent two notes at the fair

parts.note: E and F are two musical notes
a fete is a fair or garden party

explanation.surface: Someone splashes money on a couple of banknotes at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks like banknotes but means musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means exhausted or worn out, as spent can.

clue.text: The upper classes?

parts.note: reads like the aristocracy, but means pupils in the top school forms

explanation.surface: A question about the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools the sixth form is the top year group, for students aged sixteen to eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils in the highest years of a British secondary school, its uppermost classes.

clue.text: Survey to indicate one's position in the field

parts.note: to survey a topic is to cover it
to point is to indicate

explanation.surface: A land surveyor marks out a spot in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover point is a fielding position in cricket, on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a named cricket fielding position, a place a fielder stands.

clue.text: Composer has loads of energy, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the answer sounds like another phrase

parts.note: a coal porter carries loads of coal, a fuel giving energy

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain composer is very lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter was an American songwriter who wrote Anything Goes.

clue.text: Where a dancing partner shouldn't tread, if alert

definitions.text: Where a dancing partner shouldn't tread
definitions.meaning: literally the feet of the person one dances with

explanation.surface: Etiquette for a dancer: mind your partner's feet if you are awake.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's toes is an idiom for being alert, and literally where one should not step.

clue.text: He hopes to get suitable clients

definitions.text: He hopes to get suitable clients

parts.words: He hopes to get suitable clients
parts.note: suitable reads as appropriate, but means people wanting suits made

explanation.surface: A businessman wants the right sort of customers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who makes suits wants clients in need of one.

clue.text: She's in peak form in Crete

definitions.text: She's in peak form in Crete

parts.words: She's in peak form in Crete
parts.note: a woman's name that is also a mountain on a Greek island

explanation.surface: A woman is at her best on holiday in Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is a girl's name and also Mount Ida, the highest peak on Crete.

clue.text: Boy on toes, perhaps, sees secret

indicators.note: here on means placed after the other piece
perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad on tiptoe spots something hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue might suggest ERIC goes first, but here it means following; 'perhaps' signals the reshuffle of the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is known only to an inner few, so secret.

clue.text: The first mate is always cut short

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A ship's first officer always has a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Eve was the first wife, Adam's mate.

clue.text: Emergency flight

parts.note: reads like an urgent air journey, but means a flight of stairs used to get out in a blaze

explanation.surface: A plane takes off urgently.
explanation.definitionFit: An outside staircase for leaving a burning building is a flight for emergencies.

clue.text: Left in France — could be awkward

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in France feels uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche is French for left and in English means socially awkward.

clue.text: Supporters groan — it stops play

indicators.note: play means the letters are put in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fans moan when the match is halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges GROAN and IT STOPS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist can be a leading advocate or champion of a cause, a supporter.

clue.text: Try to get out of business that moves between Asian banks

indicators.note: signals one word removed from another

parts.note: business and industry are synonyms
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trader attempts to leave a firm dealing across Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river flowing through Pakistan, between banks in Asia.

clue.text: Old bar in Scotland

parts.note: to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: An ancient pub in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Oban is a port town on the west coast of Scotland, famous for its whisky distillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a town in Scotland, so the clue's 'in Scotland' points to a place found there.

clue.text: Olympian turned up where East and West meet

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and Red Sea, a meeting point of East and West

explanation.surface: An athlete appears at the crossroads of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was king of the gods who lived on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: It can't be made whole

indicators.note: made here means fashioned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something broken can never be repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact and whole both mean undamaged and complete.

clue.text: Charming Arab about to swindle the French?

indicators.note: the first word goes around the second

parts.note: taken as written
to do someone is to swindle them
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An Arab is about to cheat the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable and charming are synonyms for delightful.

clue.text: A hewer of wood and a drawer of water

definitions.meaning: a craftsman shaping wood on a lathe
the painter J M W ..., famous for watercolours

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding description of a humble labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase echoes Joshua's 'hewers of wood and drawers of water', but drawer means one who draws pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodturner shapes wood, and Turner the English artist painted watercolours.

clue.text: Extra helpings may be minute portions

definitions.meaning: parts of a minute, sixty to each

explanation.surface: Second servings might be tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Seconds are both second helpings of food and sixtieth parts of a minute.
